sentenceSets.sentence: A thorough review of the assumptions would have identified the error before it was built into every subsequent calculation.

answerChoices.reasoning: Careful means attentive to detail or cautious, but the sentence emphasizes exhaustive examination of all assumptions, not merely attentive review.
Rigorous means extremely thorough and careful, which is very close, but emphasizes strictness of methodology rather than completeness of coverage.
Detailed means containing many details, but the sentence emphasizes checking all assumptions to the point of completion, not merely detailed examination.
Comprehensive means covering all aspects or complete, which is very close to thorough, but emphasizes breadth rather than the exhaustive checking implied.
Meticulous means extremely careful about details, but the sentence's emphasis is on exhaustive coverage to catch errors, not just careful attention.
Systematic means following a method or plan, but the sentence requires a term for completeness, not just organized approach.
Analytical means examining or breaking down into parts, but the sentence emphasizes completeness of review, not analytical method.
Investigative means involving inquiry or research, but the sentence requires focus on exhaustive completion rather than investigative process.
Superficial means dealing only with surface aspects; the sentence indicates a review should examine all assumptions in depth.
Partial means incomplete or only part of a whole, opposite to the exhaustive review the sentence requires.
Hasty means done quickly without due care; the sentence requires careful checking of all assumptions.

answerChoices.reasoning: Exhaustive means extremely comprehensive or complete, which is very close to thorough, but emphasizes the extent of coverage rather than the quality of examination.
Meticulous means extremely careful about details, which is close, but emphasizes carefulness rather than exhaustiveness of checking every transaction.
Rigorous means extremely thorough and conducted carefully, which is very close, but emphasizes strictness of standards rather than completeness.
Scrupulous means extremely conscientious and careful, which is close, but emphasizes moral or ethical carefulness rather than exhaustive verification.
Attentive means giving careful attention, but the sentence requires a term for complete verification of all transactions, not just attentive observation.
Diligent means careful and persistent, but the sentence emphasizes completeness of checking, not persistence in effort.
Careful means cautious or attentive to detail, but the sentence's emphasis on checking every transaction and questioning patterns suggests exhaustiveness beyond mere carefulness.
Professional means competent or skilled, but the sentence requires a term for the scope of the examination, not professional quality.
Cursory means quick and superficial, opposite to an examination that checks every transaction and questions unusual patterns.
Selective means choosing particular items, contradicting an examination of every transaction.
Routine means standard or ordinary; the sentence describes an unusually complete examination, not routine checking.
